rule: WHEN type has to leave -> DO shrink it into the centre (0.55W -> 0.28W -> gone in 0.24 s), erase it with a centre-outward mask wipe, or scramble glyphs (+-12 deg -> 39 deg) and hard-switch; overlap the outgoing ghost under the incoming object for 2-4 frames. NEVER opacity-fade in place (the one fade, M958 1.63-1.90 at 90% -> 5%, is paired with outward push and badge growth, so it reads as being replaced by the icon). -> BECAUSE the eye keeps tracking an object instead of seeing a gap. (M947, M958)

WHEN the next object IS the continuation of the sentence -> DO open a gap in the line exactly the width of the incoming badge (M958: sides slide ~42 px / 0.06W fast-out, badge grows 0.04W -> 0.07W monotonic, second badge emerges from behind the first at 1.27) -> BECAUSE the icons stand in for words, so the line finishes as a pictogram; growth is monotonic, no 112% pop. (M958, M947 badge)

WHEN an object must change identity (two badges -> a cluster, a ring of letters -> a title) -> DO a ONE-FRAME hard switch plus a 5-frame recolour/shape settle (M958 1.90: muddy #69433C node -> red by 2.07; M947 3.10: scramble -> exactly 6 glyphs) and never draw in-between morph frames -> BECAUSE hard switches read as designed; gooey morphs read as generated. (M947, M958)

WHEN a letter ring or token ring is needed -> DO place items on an ellipse around the hero (M956: centre (0.52,0.62), radii 0.10W x 0.15H, upper tokens 0.03W / lower 0.06W as depth), 9 items entering 1-2 frames apart each at its own ring slot, flash bright (#fffaff core + glow) for ~0.13 s then settle to a plain fill, rotate clockwise 1-3 px/frame with glyphs staying upright, keep 1-2 tokens glowing -> BECAUSE the ring counts the inventory visibly and never reads as particle dust. (M956, M947)

WHEN an orbit/stroke accent is used -> DO enter it at maximum thickness (0.11H) from the corner, whip its head 0.8W in 0.10 s, thin it to 0.03H over 0.67 s, circle OUTSIDE the text, exit through the frame edge -> BECAUSE the stroke is a camera-like frame for the word and never competes with it. (M947)

WHEN a number must "resolve" -> DO roll through discrete values, one per frame, 15-23 steps in 0.5-0.9 s, step sizes decaying to ~0.07 at the end so it lands rather than stops (M954 $86.94 -> $100.00 in 16 frames; M958 2.71 -> 522.14 in 23 events) -> BECAUSE the viewer feels the amount arrive. Hero claims end on round values (100.00, 10% a name, 120+), product-data fields end on specific un-round values (522.14, 119 a name, 112/500) so the screen feels real. (M954, M955, M958)

WHEN a counter or percentage steps -> DO skip values (M955 skips 5%, M954 jumps 1.78/1.84/1.56 between 0.6-0.9 steps), hold 1-3 frames per value, and never tween digits -> BECAUSE uneven steps look measured; smooth rolls look like a compositing tool presets. (M954, M955, M958)

WHEN a number is the hero -> DO defocus only its edge glyphs (M954: "$" and final "0" blurred ~12 px, centre digits sharp until 1.07-1.20) and pull the view back 0.91W -> 0.63W in 0.20 s -> BECAUSE focus lands on the digits that carry the message. (M954)

WHEN a headline must hold for >1 s -> DO keep something else alive underneath (M955: a name +1/+2 every 1-3 frames for 1.87 s, mascot bob, blink at 1.07-1.27; M947/M953 text shrinks 9% over 0.6 s; M949 drifts at 1-30 px/step; never a frozen hold) -> BECAUSE a locked frame reads as slideware. (M947, M949, M953, M955)

WHEN a 3D phone/device is the hero -> DO crop it (top corners off-frame, bottom at y 0.97, screen ~0.39W), start at yaw -54 deg / x-tilt 29 / roll 11 and reach -9 / 24 / 2 in 6 held poses within 0.40 s under ~1870 px perspective, keep side thickness visible early (0.05W -> 0.01W), then drift; put the headline BEHIND the device and a big sparkle IN FRONT of its corner; UI is one perspective plane. Or fake 3D with stepped 2D camera jumps (M957: 0.13/0.20/0.23, 1.8x, dive via held steps) -> BECAUSE "a product you could hold" needs depth cues, not a flat rectangle. (M955, M957)

WHEN a screen is shown flat -> DO give it a camera: scale the window itself 0.70W -> 0.78W over 1.2 s (M953), never scale bars/cards separately; or pan the whole dark dashboard 0.33W left with 79% of it in 0.27 s and crop the left edge (M956); keep blurred secondary panels (7-15 px) -> BECAUSE parallax and focus tell the eye which panel is live. (M953, M956, M958)

WHEN a cursor enters -> DO make it oversized (M953 1.55-2.2x; M956 0.36W; M959 5.1x, mostly off-frame, blurred) and scale it about its TIP while it decelerates onto the target with 60% of the travel in the first frame step and a 0.5-0.9 s creep; never a hold before the click -> BECAUSE the cursor reads as thrown at the screen and the tip stays the anchor. (M953, M956, M959, M948)

WHEN a click happens -> DO a 2-3 frame press (cursor and target to 0.72-0.80 scale; M956 button -29% with arrow lagging one frame; M959 cursor -13% + tip down 0.03H), a hard colour step on the target, a bar dip of 15% recovering in 0.14 s, and a glow that decays over 0.3 s (peak 35 px blur @40% for M956); NEVER ripple rings or a white screen flash. For a hero CTA add one frame of label smear (95 px, 0.44W) and a swell of 1.02 -> BECAUSE the click is felt in the object, not announced by a graphic. (M953, M956, M959)

WHEN each of several cursors/agents appears -> DO give each ONE job and start them on different frames (M953: a name drags a card, a name recolours bars twice, a name clicks a heading; events every ~0.3 s from 1.94 to 2.74), name pills on each, cursors jump rather than interpolate across the cut -> BECAUSE "live collaboration" is shown as simultaneous cause and effect. (M953)

WHEN a prompt is typed -> DO type at human cadence (M949: 1.2 chars/step, 0.02-0.07 s inside words, 0.10 before an ending letter, 0.20 before a space, "le" together), 0.14H cap at large scale, a tall thin caret (0.008W x 0.25H) that never blinks and jumps on each glyph, a continuous leftward slide that accelerates 0.006W -> 0.027W per step, and snap scale by hard cut (x0.42) in the same frame the copy jumps ahead ("into one" appears at once). Keep the typo. For a UI field type 2-3 chars/frame with the newest 1-3 glyphs in the accent for 1 frame (M956) -> BECAUSE the viewer authors the sentence and the snap converts overflow into a committed, frame-fitting line. (M949, M956)

WHEN scale changes in a text beat -> DO hard-cut it (M949: 1.00 -> 0.42 -> 1.57x of large), not tween; and pair the cut with a content jump in the same frame -> BECAUSE a zoom interpolation announces itself; a snap is read as editing. Same for camera: M956 uses an accelerating ease-in push (2.80-3.44) then a DISCONTINUOUS jump to the macro (0.04W -> 0.27W). (M949, M956)

WHEN you need an end state / CTA -> DO stop on an object mid-motion that implies the viewer's next move: M959 shrinks button/bracket/cursor to 0.74/0.76/0.75 with the biggest step on the final frame and cuts to white before release; M949 ends 0.11 s into the send arrow's arrival, mid-slide, never showing the send; M958 ends with Buy pulsing and the camera still moving; M955 ends with the badge still shrinking on the last frame. -> BECAUSE the action transfers to the viewer. (M949, M955, M958, M959)

WHEN an icon/brand mark is the last thing -> DO cut hard to a flat ground (white/cream), start the mark at 1.5-1.9x, and settle it over 2.5 s with an exponential curve (1.864 -> 1.449 in 0.13 s -> 1.10 @2.4 -> 1.0 @4.0), no overshoot, no tagline, no fade; or a one-frame word card (M957 "Now", 0.10H, regular, left of centre at x 0.46, 3 px blur) as a chapter hand-off -> BECAUSE the settle is slow enough to feel alive and the single frame carries into the next scene. (M959, M957)

WHEN a title sits on its final slot -> DO set it OFF-CENTRE (x 0.47, y 0.50) with a gradient clipped to glyphs and add colour washes only at the end (lavender lower-left, cyan upper-right, centre white) -> BECAUSE an exact-centre title reads as default; the washes arrive with the resolve as the reward. (M947, M948)

WHEN a scene is a montage of styles -> DO strobe plates at 4 source frames (0.067 s) with a 2-frame first flash, 14 plates then repeats, hard cuts, zero fade, entering and exiting on hard cuts; the product glyph must not bloom into it (M948: glyph peaks at 0.30W x 0.46H and the cut lands on max growth velocity) -> BECAUSE a strobe at ~15 plates/s feels like range, and a bloom would soften the cut. (M948)
safety_note: Historical rapid-plate observation, not a safe-flash threshold. Review opposing luminance changes and general/red thresholds at the largest viewing size and while looping; omit the strobe if unverified. https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/three-flashes-or-below-threshold.html

rule: WHEN items are collected (M948 four references -> folder -> gallery) -> DO enter from four different edges on ~0.10 s staggers (one as a huge blurred foreground square 0.29 -> 0.39W), grab with a 0.03H lift (no halo), drag on a curved path while scaling 0.14 -> 0.09W, hide the stack in a glass folder, vanish the folder on a single frame, then spring the result (card 0.31H -> 0.58H, thumbnails on 2-frame staggers with 0.06H overshoot) -> BECAUSE overshoot saved for one payoff moment reads as reward; everywhere else decelerate with no bounce. (M948)

WHEN objects are consumed (M954 monster) -> DO shrink them toward the mouth 6-10 frames with rotation (+5 -> +18 deg) and darkening, grow the mouth over them rather than flying them in, show eyes/teeth without a pop, keep pupils the same colour as the head, and push in to 0.80W then pull back (never end on black) -> BECAUSE character beats come from flat shapes with deliberate asymmetry, not 3D polish. (M954)

WHEN a world changes (new product, new ground) -> DO hard-cut and carry ONE literal object, word, caret, or UI across (M947->M948 title + washes + banana at (0.70, 0.50); M948->M949 gray caret centre; M957->M958 "Now"; M958->M959 the last terminal frame held 1 frame) -> BECAUSE a film of 15 different looks still reads as one piece. (M947-M949, M957-M959)

WHEN stepping motion (the "on twos" look) -> DO hold every pose 2 source frames and place all onsets on those steps; keep the step across typing, translation, scale and stroke. Only the non-step exceptions are product surfaces (camera moves in M953/M958 are smooth at 30 fps) -> BECAUSE a consistent frame rhythm across the film is what makes it feel hand-animated rather than interpolated. (M947, M948, M949)

WHEN a hard cut hides a camera: land it at maximum velocity or just before a hold (M948 1.23 mid-swell; M954 2.07 after scan fade 0.73/0.50/0.30/0.13; M958 3.04 with the circle at 0.25W and cream right; M959 1.53 on the largest shrink step) -> BECAUSE motion continues in the viewer's head across the cut.

WHEN a state change should read as "engineered" and not "animated" -> DO a hard cut on an exact frame into ~90% of the final state, then a 3-10% ease-out settle over 7-14 frames (disc r108 -> r120 in 0.5 s; 3 rings .48 -> .45; 13 rings drift +3% R; tangent bars +66% in 7 frames; dial arcs decay x0.57/frame) BECAUSE the cut gives impact and the tiny settle gives life without a morph. (M962)

WHEN a sequence of diagrams/CAD states cuts on a beat -> DO a constant cut interval (10 frames = 0.333 s at 30 fps for four consecutive cuts), each state complete at the cut (dashes full length, labels present) with only nodes/handles arriving 1-3 frames later in two waves (even ticks +1 frame, odd +2) BECAUSE the viewer reads cut = beat and detail as an echo. (M962)

WHEN you need a through-line object -> DO make one object (a 22 px dot, 3.1% H) the carrier: it rides the end of the typed line, steps through every state, and in the next moment IS the seed of the product shape; end the moment with it displaced (x 0.28) so the next opens at that position (0.27) BECAUSE a continuous object makes two edits feel like one film. (M962 -> M963)

WHEN text types in -> DO keep the typed line centred and move any carrier (dot, caret, emblem) with its live right edge on every event (dot +0.1 W across 18 chars, even on space steps) BECAUSE it reads as composing now, and nothing is anchored to a fixed spot. (M962, M969)

WHEN typing copy -> DO use an authored rhythm: bursts of 1-frame (or 2-frame at 15 fps) letters, 6-10 frame pauses after spaces ("This " held 10 frames, "This is " held 6), skipped intermediate states ("Th" never shown, "my" arrives as 2 letters, "l" never alone before "le"), and a slower last word (letters every 3 frames after fast whole words) BECAUSE metronomic one-char-per-frame typing is the clearest slop tell. (M962, M965, M966, M969)

WHEN removing a line -> DO wipe it (a clip edge sweeping through the glyphs while the line slides the same direction, 5 frames, accelerating) or vanish words in hard steps 2 frames apart; use per-letter backspace only when erasing is part of the story (brand name erased as petals swirl into a mark) BECAUSE mid-glyph cuts feel physical. (M962, M964, M968)

WHEN words arrive in a headline -> DO pop each word whole on one frame (no fade, no blur, no typing), offset ~0.04 H low or 16 px to the entry side, decay x0.6-0.72 per frame (90% in 5 frames at 24 fps), no overshoot, and slide the whole line so the group stays centred BECAUSE the viewer reads one beat per word and the line is never off-balance. (M964, M967)

WHEN a new word arrives and needs attention -> DO give it the ONE accent for the shortest time that registers (24 fps: 1-2 frames in cycling flash colours; 30 fps: 6 frames purple; 60 fps: 0.28 s linear violet -> ink) and settle to ink BECAUSE colour = "this is arriving", and the frame stays monochrome at rest. (M966, M967, M973, M974)

WHEN spending a colour budget -> DO keep text/ink and ground monochrome and spend colour on (a) arrival, (b) the payoff of the whole film (M963 gets its only colour in the last demo, 0.9 s, sparse ~5% orange), (c) block/brand marks BECAUSE colour used once reads as an event. (M963, M964, M967)

WHEN picking a film clock -> DO choose one and hold it for the whole moment: 2-frame holds on even frames (15 fps look) for indie/technical sets (M967-M969), 24 fps with smooth moves + stepped reveals for a product-explainer (M964-M966), 30 fps for CAD idents (M962/963), 60 fps smooth for brand-morph and UI zoom (M973/974) BECAUSE mixed step rates look like a bug. (M962-M974)

WHEN two scales must be shown (cluster -> close-up -> ribbon) -> DO hard-cut in ONE frame (0.037 W -> 0.136 W = 3.7x; then back to 0.035 W) and let the background keep its own scale and drift (tiles 73 px pitch, 0.07 W/s left) BECAUSE a cut says "different distance", a zoom says "camera", and the background not scaling keeps the world stable. (M964)

WHEN dissolving a field into a logo or screen -> DO use real hard-edged cells (1.5-2.5% W) with stepped coverage (90% -> 60% -> 35% -> 10% -> 0 over 0.33 s, opening from the bottom; or 12x12 -> 15x15 -> 17x17 -> 20x20 grid retreating to corners in 3 steps over 0.27 s), never opacity BECAUSE pixel occlusion reads as digital craft and the cells carry the brand colour. (M965, M968)

WHEN revealing a logo -> DO enter oversized and blurred and scale DOWN (0.28 W -> 0.10 W, blur 18 -> 0 px, halving the excess every 2 frames, 0.33 s), or hold full at frame 0 and shrink with exponential ease-out (scaleX 1.46 -> 1.0 in 8 frames, creep to 0.96, then accelerate and cut on one frame); never scale up from zero or fade BECAUSE "arrives from the camera" reads as authority. (M968, M965)

WHEN transforming one identity into another -> DO flip per glyph left to right at ~2 frames (60 fps) per glyph: old glyph squashes up to a hairline (3 frames), new grows from a baseline hairline in 6-8 frames, two thin strokes visible at different heights; fixed left anchor (x 0.49) so the eye never travels; add an anticipation spread (+26% tracking over 0.19 s) before the second flip BECAUSE the viewer sees both names from one lockup. (M973)

WHEN swapping icons -> DO spin the old one up (accelerating to ~30 deg/frame while shrinking to 0.87x), cross-dissolve over 8 frames on a shared centre, and let the new one inherit the spin (-139 deg decelerating to 0 over 0.26 s) with one 4% overshoot at 0.87 s BECAUSE conserved momentum makes a dissolve feel like one object changing. (M973)

WHEN diving from the brand into the product -> DO scale the camera from frame 0 with no hold at a constant octave rate (1 -> 21.9 in 0.53 s, ~x1.5-2 per 0.067 s), translate toward a feature of the logo (the underscore) not the centre, so it exits the frame edge, let the feature become a near-full-frame white mass, fade the mass in place in 3 frames, show 3 blank frames, then zoom a larger container out to rest (0.05/0.98 -> 0.25/0.78 in 0.62 s, stroke 10 -> 4 px) BECAUSE the logo is felt to contain the product. (M974)

WHEN a UI line is longer than the box -> DO make the container wider than the frame (1.78 W), type per glyph with a +25 -> -24 -> 0 px wave (0.035 H, 14-frame life, colour violet -> ink in 17 frames), and pan the whole UI as one group (eased, peak mid-typing) so controls arrive by the pan, never a pop BECAUSE the type has liveliness without a cursor or wrap and the pan "reveals" the action. (M974)

WHEN showing a cursor in a prompt UI -> DO bring it in late (0.7 s before the end of typing), move it in 2-frame steps with decay x0.72, bending toward vertical, park it before the action, no hover/press/ripple; show the click as the next container replacing the bar at full size on a ground that shifts one step darker/greyer (#ECEBE3 -> #C4C2B1) BECAUSE the cut is the proof and nothing wastes a frame. (M969)

WHEN a button must react -> DO cross-colour it: disc black -> #969696 -> white while the arrow goes white -> same grey (invisible at the midpoint) -> black, 0.28 s, no scale BECAUSE it reads "sent" without a cartoon press. (M974)

WHEN demonstrating a parameter system -> DO use a fixed lattice where nothing moves except per-dot size, opacity or colour, driven by a spatial function (radial wave 20 px/frame, row band, ring, left/right sweep, radial colour front at ring n start 6.10 + 0.085n s), 0.8-0.9 s per demo, amplitudes escalating per repetition (6.6/7.7/8.4 px), base 4.7 px vs large 13.3 px BECAUSE the viewer infers a system with knobs from one object. (M963)

WHEN labelling the active parameter -> DO scroll the whole list one line (20 px = line height) behind a FIXED bullet in 0.33 s with a snap (53% of travel in one frame, 93% in four), dip the bullet 13 -> 9 -> 13.8 px on the same beat, change the word colour only (#A3A3A3 <-> #000, never weight) BECAUSE the fixed anchor keeps the reader's eye in place. (M963)

WHEN a title must feel like an act break -> DO squeeze the old act with ease-in (scale 0.98 -> 0.91 -> 0.74 -> 0.30 in 4 steps), jitter 6 px strips +-1 px for 0.4 s, hard cut, then resolve the new, bigger type word by word (0.11 H -> 0.16 H), each from 0.73 scale in the accent to 1.0 white in ~0.2 s BECAUSE the anticipation + size jump make the cut an event. (M967)

WHEN a reel of categories flips -> DO swap card + badge together on a syncopated 4/2-frame pattern (13 swaps in 1.4 s), no crossfade, same container scale track (0.30 -> 1.0 over 0.8 s ease-out), the outer words creep apart behind it BECAUSE the viewer reads "many" without reading each. (M967)

WHEN ending a moment -> DO end mid-motion (phrases still sliding, man still rising, badge still turning, dial half-exited), or on a one-frame new element (capsule, card, 8-block grid + green bar) BECAUSE the next moment picks up the momentum and the last frame matches the first frame of the next. (M962, M963, M965, M966, M969, M973, M974)

WHEN holding for the payoff -> DO hold only after the payoff lands (lockup 0.67 s static, headline 0.67 s with a solid caret) and keep micro-drift everywhere else (tile drift 0.07 W/s, creeping word spread to 0.14 W, orb breathing 0.255 -> 0.26 W, 0.4% shrink steps) BECAUSE nothing freezes except what must be read. (M964, M966, M967, M968, M969)

WHEN text onsets are synced -> DO land each onset on the spoken word (M967 voice 0.13-3.83 s, words at 0.07/0.33/0.47, then 2.33/2.47/2.67) and spread the gaps to the speech (4, 6 frames) BECAUSE the viewer hears the headline as a list. (M964, M967, M968)

WHEN scaling type by role -> DO use technical annotation 1.3% H (9 px), ident title 4.4% H (32 px), phrase 5-6.4% H, menu 2.4% H, UI prompt 4% H, act-one word 11% H, act-two word 16% H, brand word 21% H (154 px); weights 400-650, never bold, tracking -0.4 px at small sizes to -6 px at 154 px BECAUSE role-based scale gives hierarchy without bold. (M962-M969)

WHEN a camera/parallax pan is needed -> DO use two pushes with different accelerations (fast-then-slow, then accelerate to a peak 0.025 W/frame and settle) and 2-2.4x parallax between layers (tiles > diagram > orb), exits clipped by the frame edge, staggered (text 1.54 s, grid 1.92 s), never one ease BECAUSE a single ease looks like a keyframe, two pushes look like a camera operator. (M966)

WHEN you need a generative texture -> DO use flat, hard squares on a grid (73 px or 14.6 px pitch, 3-14 px cells, #2D2121 on #1E1212, clusters with holes) born in place and never moving or flickering, delayed 0.2 s after the headline lands BECAUSE texture without competition. (M964, M967)

WHEN a container replaces a screen -> DO contract the old container with ease-in (0.70 -> 0.64 W, -9%) then replace it outright with the next container at full size (0.83 x 0.85) and a faint halo; a 1-frame empty capsule/card is a placeholder for the next scene BECAUSE it sets up the next moment. (M966, M969)
